title: Auer wins wet Nürburgring Race 1 as Mercedes sweep the top four
dek: Lucas Auer won Race 1 at the Nürburgring from pole for Mercedes-AMG, ahead of di Resta and Wickens, after a late rain shower ruined the slick-tyre gambles of Farfus and Ekström.

chapters.title: A title fight with five races to run
text: The Nürburgring brought round seven of the 2017 DTM season, and Saturday's race was the 13th of 18. Mattias Ekström arrived as championship leader with 128 points, 14 clear of his Audi team-mate René Rast, while Lucas Auer, the best-placed Mercedes driver, was sixth on 99, 29 points off the top. Auer had won twice earlier in the year but had also collected several blank weekends since, and he came to the Eifel needing a clean result.

Audi came with a handicap. Under the series' performance weights the Audi RS 5 DTMs were carrying 25kg more than the BMWs, and Ekström said openly before the weekend that qualifying in particular would be extremely difficult. The previous round at Zandvoort had been shared between BMW and Audi, with Timo Glock winning Race 1 from pole and Mike Rockenfeller taking Race 2.

The Nürburgring is famous for its changeable weather, and the build-up followed the script. Rain on Friday and a damp Saturday morning set the tone, and the weekend looked likely to be decided as much by tyre choice as by pace.

chapters.title: Auer takes pole on the last lap
text: Qualifying began on a wet track and the times fell steadily as it dried. Lucas Auer timed his run best, setting 1:25.968 at the end of the session to take pole position for Mercedes-AMG by 0.099 seconds from Marco Wittmann's BMW, who recorded 1:26.067. Robert Wickens, in the second Mercedes, was 0.410 seconds off the pace in third.

Augusto Farfus took fourth for BMW on 1:26.484, ahead of Paul di Resta's Mercedes (1:26.912) and Tom Blomqvist's BMW (1:27.044). René Rast was the best Audi in seventh, 1.094 seconds behind Auer, with Timo Glock eighth, Maro Engel ninth and Maxime Martin tenth.

It was a poor session for the championship leader. Mattias Ekström could only manage 11th on 1:27.682, 1.714 seconds slower than Auer, with Rockenfeller 12th, Gary Paffett 13th and Jamie Green 14th. Bruno Spengler and Edoardo Mortara were 15th and 16th, Nico Müller 17th, and Loïc Duval at the back, 3.306 seconds off pole. The grid for the race was the qualifying order.

chapters.title: Farfus leaps into the lead
text: Rain returned to the Eifel shortly before the start, and all 18 cars lined up on wet tyres. Farfus made the best getaway from fourth on the grid, passed Wittmann and pole-sitter Auer, and led into the first corner, with Auer, di Resta and Wickens behind him.

The Brazilian dominated the opening half of the race and at one point led by about seven seconds as the track began to dry. Further back, Ekström climbed from 11th into the top seven, and Rast and Engel touched at Turn 2 in a fight for position; Rast was given a warning, his third of the year, which carried a five-place grid penalty into Sunday's race.

chapters.title: The rain returns on the slicks
text: By the middle of the race a dry line had formed, and the field began to take its mandatory stop. Blomqvist, Rockenfeller and Müller were among the first to change to slick tyres, with Wittmann and Paffett following a lap later. Leader Farfus and Ekström came in as well, only for the rain to return almost as they rejoined; both were left struggling on slicks and Farfus was back in for wets within a couple of laps, with Ekström making a second stop later.

The drivers who had stayed out on their original wets were handed the top positions. Auer and Wickens stopped together at the end of lap 24 for new rain tyres. Di Resta stayed out slightly longer and emerged in front after a slower stop, while Auer ran wide and lost time to Mortara, who had not yet stopped. Engel and Green held brief spells at the front before their own stops, and Paffett, on slicks, stayed out until the flag.

chapters.title: Di Resta slows and Auer wins
text: Di Resta led the closing laps with Auer and Wickens close behind, and with the finish in sight the Scot slowed on the run to the final chicane. Auer went through to the lead and won in 54:12.443, 0.794 seconds clear of his team-mate, with Wickens 1.568 seconds back in third. Engel was fourth, 5.344 seconds from the winner, and Mercedes held the top four places; all six of the manufacturer's cars finished in the top ten.

Rast was fifth and the best of the rest, 9.758 seconds behind, with Green sixth for Audi, Mortara seventh, Farfus eighth after his second stop, Wittmann ninth and Paffett tenth, one of the few still on slicks at the end. Ekström finished 15th, a lap down, and scored nothing. Auer called it a brutal day of rain, drying and rain again, and the result lifted him to second in the standings on 127 points, one behind Ekström, with Rast third on 124.

facts.v: Auer, di Resta, Wickens and Engel finished first to fourth, and all six Mercedes-AMG cars were in the top ten.
